EXHIBIT A

Type 1 Narrative

The lot area of 2820 W. Diversey Ave., Chicago, IL 60647 (the “Subject Property”) is 3,125 SF
per the survey, which is attached hereto as Appendix 1. The Subject Property is improved with a
2-story approximately 2,183 SF brick masonry building. Attached hereto as Appendix 2 is a plant
set of the existing building. The plan set is comprised of a site plan, 1* floor plan, 2"4 floor plan,
front/south elevation, rear/north elevation, east elevation and west elevation.

Even though this application does not qualify as a Type | zoning map amendment application,
the Applicant elects to submit this application as a Type | application pursuant to Section 17-13-
0302-A-2. The application does not qualify as a Type 1 for the following reasons. First, rezoning
the Subject Property from B3-1 to B2-2 will not result in a floor area ratio that is 2 or more times
higher than the Subject Property’s zoning classification. (Zoning Ordinance, Section 17-13-0302-
A-1-(a)). The maximum FAR in the B3-1 district is 1.2 and the maximum FAR in the B2-2
district is 2.2. Therefore, the FAR in the B2-2 district is less than 2.4 (i.e., 2 multiplied by 1.2
equals 2.4). The existing building’s FAR is 0.69 (i.e., 2,183 SF + 3,125 FT = 0.69). Second,
rezoning the Subject Property from B3-1 to B2-2 will not result in a rezoning from a zoning
district that does not impose maximum height limits to a zoning district that does impose
maximum height limits. (Zoning Ordinance, Section 17-13-0302-A-1-(b)). Third, rezoning the
Subject Property will not result in a rezoning from a zoning district that does not allow
household living uses to a zoning district that does allow household living uses. (Zoning
Ordinance, Section 17-13-0302-A-1-(c)). Fourth, rezoning the Subject Property does not trigger
Section 17-13-0302-A-1-(e) or (f). Even though the application does not qualify for a Type 1
application, the Applicant elects to submit this application as a Type 1 application pursuant to
Section 17-13-0302-A-2.

(a) Floor Area Ratio. In the B2-2 district, the maximum FAR is 2.2. The proposed
project (i.e., conforming the existing building) will have an FAR of 0.69. Therefore, the project
will conform to the FAR regulations.

(b) Density (lot area per dwelling unit). In the B3-1 district, the minimum lot area
required for the four (4) existing Efficiency Units is 10,000 ft? (i.e., 4 Efficiency Units

multiplied by 2,500 ft? equals 10,000 ft.2). The Subject Property is 3,125 ft.?. In the B2-2 district,
the minimum lot area required for the four (4) existing Efficiency Units is 2,800 ft”. If the
Subject Property is rezoned to the B2-2 district, then the current use will conform to the use and
minimum lot area regulations under the Zoning Ordinance.

The existing Efficiency Units conform to the minimum average dwelling unit size.
(Zoning Ordinance, Section 17-3-0409). The gross residential floor area developed on a lot
divided by the total number of dwelling units on such lot may not be less than 500 square feet.
Pursuant to the floor plans, the existing gross residential floor area is 2,183 ft.’. Based on this
floor area, the average dwelling unit size is 545 ft.? which is greater than the minimum 500 ft.
(ie., 2,183 ft.2 [gross residential floor area] divided by 4 [total number of dwelling units] equals
545 ft).

The limitation on the maximum number of Efficiency Units under Section 17-3-0410-A
does not apply to the Subject Property because the Subject Property is located within 660 feet of
a CTA bus line corridor or road segment listed in Table 17-17-0400-B. The Subject Property is
located adjacent to the Diversey Avenue between Kedzie Avenue and N. Lakeshore Dr. segment.
(Zoning Ordinance, Section 17-3-0410-B-2).

(c) Off-street Parking. In the B2-2 district, the minimum parking requirement for the
existing Efficiency Units use is one (1) vehicle space per unit resulting in a minimum parking
requirement of four (4) vehicle spaces. (Zoning Ordinance, Section 17-10-0207-C). There are
two (2) existing off-street parking spaces at the rear of the Subject Property. However, pursuant
to Section 17-10-0102-B-1-(a), in the B districts, minimum off-street automobile parking ratios
may be reduced by up to 100 percent from the otherwise applicable standards for reuse of
existing structures located within 1,320 feet of a CTA bus line corridor roadway segment listed in
Table 17-17-0400-B. The proposed reuse of the existing building for the existing Efficiency
Units at 2820 W. Diversey Ave. is located directly along the CTA’s Diversey Avenue between
Kedzie Avenue and N. Lakeshore Dr. segment bus line corridor and, thus, less than 1,320 feet of
this eligible segment. Therefore, the minimum off-street parking requirement is zero (0).

(d) Setbacks. With respect to the other applicable zoning regulations, the existing
building conforms with the minimum setback requirements in the B2-2 district. The minimum
front setback requirement is none. (Zoning Ordinance, Section 17-3-0404). The minimum rear
setback requirement is 30 feet and the existing rear setback is 66.9 feet per the survey. (Zoning
Ordinance, Section 17-3-0405). The minimum side setback requirement is none. (Zoning
Ordinance, Section 17-3-0406). The Applicant does not seek to make any changes to the existing
setbacks.

(e) Building Height. The existing two-story building height is 26’-6” in height which
is less than the maximum building height of 45 feet. (Zoning Ordinance, Section 17-3-0408-A).
The Applicant does not seek to make any changes to the existing building height.

Supplemental Information

The primary reason the Applicant seeks to rezone the Subject Property is to ensure that the
residential tenants, who have resided in the building for several years and pay below-market
affordable rents, will not lose their home. The tenant who occupies one of the first-floor units is
an elderly African-American male veteran. This tenant serves as the de facto property manager
and works closely with the Applicant to ensure that the building is well maintained. If the
application to rezone the Subject Property is not approved by the City Council, then all of the
tenants will be required to vacate the building and, thus, lose their below-market affordable
rental units.

The prior owner obtained title to the Subject Property on December 6, 2021. The Applicant
obtained title to the Subject Property on December 29, 2022, via a foreclosure proceeding. The
Applicant was the mortgagee. Prior to the Applicant obtaining title, the Subject Property was

used for Dwelling Units located below the second floor-Multi-Unit (3+ units) Residential.
Specifically, there were four Efficiency Units, all of which were occupied by tenants. Two of the
units are located on the first floor and two of the units are located on the second floor. One of the
units on the first floor has been and continues to be occupied by an elderly African-American
male veteran. Each of the tenants are members of a minority group, employed, and work in the
City of Chicago.

When the Applicant obtained title to the Subject Property in December 2022, all four of the
residential units were occupied and all of the tenants were paying below-market affordable rents.
Since the Applicant obtained title to the Subject Property, all of the tenants have remained in
possession of their units and the Applicant has maintained the below-market affordable rents.
According to comparative rental market analysis prepared by Compass dated July 15, 2025 (the
“Comparative Rental Market Report”), within a 1-mile radius of the Subject Property, the
average monthly rent for a similar dwelling is $1,499 which is equivalent to an average annual
rent of $17,988. Attached hereto as Appendix 3 is the Comparative Rental Market Report. The
following is the annual rent for each of the residential units as of 2025: (a) Unit 1F: $7,200; (b)
Unit 1R: $8,400; (c) Unit 2F: $16,200 and (d) Unit 2R: $13,800. Attached hereto as Appendix 4
is the rent roll spread sheet. Therefore, Applicant is renting all of the units for below-market rents
per the Comparative Rental Market Report.

On August 16, 2022, the City of Chicago filed a complaint for equitable and other relief against
the prior owner.' The Applicant was named as a party defendant because as of the date of filing
the complaint, the Applicant was the mortgagee. Among other things, the complaint alleges that
on or about May 13, 2022, a first-floor commercial space was converted into two separate
Efficiency Units and the second floor was converted into separate two Efficiency Units. The
complaint alleges that no special use approval was obtained for the two Efficiency Units below
the first floor. The complaint alleges that the two Efficiency Units below the first floor are
prohibited uses in the B3-1 district because a special use permit was not obtained for the use.
Furthermore, the complaint alleges that the minimum lot area is 2,500 ft.2 per dwelling unit and
that the Subject Property does not comply with the minimum lot area requirement. In part, the
court proceedings are pending the outcome of this zoning map amendment application.

The Applicant seeks to rezone the Subject Property from B3-1, Community Shopping District, to
B2-2, Neighborhood Mixed-Use District. In the B3-1 district, Dwelling Units located below the
second-floor-Multi-Unit (3+ units) Residential require special use approval. In the B2-2 district,
this type of use is permitted by-right.

On Diversey Ave. between N. California Ave. and N. Richmond, there are several multi-unit
residential buildings with dwelling units located below the first floor.

In summary, the Applicant seeks to rezone the Subject Property from B3-1 to B2-2 to conform
the existing residential use, which predated the Applicant’s ownership of the Subject Property,
with the Zoning Ordinance. Rezoning the Subject Property will ensure that the tenants do not
lose their home and below-market affordable rental units.

' The caption of the complaint is City of Chicago v. MN Real Properties LLC, et. al., No. 22 M1 401149.
